legend: Ilya is working for the company that constructs robots. Ilya writes programs for entertainment robots, and his current project is "Bob", a new-generation game robot. Ilya's boss wants to know his progress so far. Especially he is interested if Bob is better at playing different games than the previous model, "Alice".

So now Ilya wants to compare his robots' performance in a simple game called "1-2-3". This game is similar to the "Rock-Paper-Scissors" game: both robots secretly choose a number from the set {1, 2, 3} and say it at the same moment. If both robots choose the same number, then it's a draw and noone gets any points. But if chosen numbers are different, then one of the robots gets a point: 3 beats 2, 2 beats 1 and 1 beats 3.
Both robots' programs make them choose their numbers in such a way that their choice in (i + 1)-th game depends only on the numbers chosen by them in i-th game.

Ilya knows that the robots will play k games, Alice will choose number a in the first game, and Bob will choose b in the first game. He also knows both robots' programs and can tell what each robot will choose depending on their choices in previous game. Ilya doesn't want to wait until robots play all k games, so he asks you to predict the number of points they will have after the final game.
input: The first line contains three numbers k, a, b (1 ≤ k ≤ 1018, 1 ≤ a, b ≤ 3).
Then 3 lines follow, i-th of them containing 3 numbers Ai, 1, Ai, 2, Ai, 3, where Ai, j represents Alice's choice in the game if Alice chose i in previous game and Bob chose j (1 ≤ Ai, j ≤ 3).
Then 3 lines follow, i-th of them containing 3 numbers Bi, 1, Bi, 2, Bi, 3, where Bi, j represents Bob's choice in the game if Alice chose i in previous game and Bob chose j (1 ≤ Bi, j ≤ 3).
output: Print two numbers. First of them has to be equal to the number of points Alice will have, and second of them must be Bob's score after k games.
note: In the second example game goes like this:
The fourth and the seventh game are won by Bob, the first game is draw and the rest are won by Alice.

legend.ai: Ilya 正在一家制造机器人的公司工作。Ilya 为娱乐机器人编写程序，而他当前的项目是“Bob”，一种新一代的游戏机器人。Ilya 的老板想了解他目前的进展，尤其关心 Bob 在进行不同游戏时是否比之前的模型“Alice”更出色。
因此，现在 Ilya 想在一个名为“1-2-3”的简单游戏中比较他的机器人性能。这个游戏类似于“石头剪刀布”：两个机器人都秘密地从集合 {1, 2, 3} 中选择一个数字，并在同一时刻说出这个数字。如果两个机器人选择了相同的数字，则为平局，双方都不得分。但如果选择的数字不同，则其中一个机器人得一分：3 胜 2，2 胜 1，1 胜 3。
两台机器人的程序会让它们按照这样的方式选择数字：它们在第 \(i+1\) 局中的选择只取决于它们在第 \(i\) 局中选择的数字。
Ilya 知道机器人将进行 \(k\) 局游戏，Alice 在第一局选择数字 \(a\)，Bob 在第一局选择数字 \(b\)。他还知道两台机器人的程序，并且可以根据它们上一局的选择判断每台机器人将选择什么。Ilya 不想等到机器人完成全部 \(k\) 局游戏，因此他请你预测它们在最后一局结束后各自获得的分数。

input.ai: 接下来有 3 行，第 \(i\) 行包含 3 个数字 \(A_{i,1}\)、\(A_{i,2}\)、\(A_{i,3}\)，其中 \(A_{i,j}\) 表示 Alice 在上一局选择 \(i\) 且 Bob 选择 \(j\) 时，Alice 在本局的选择（\(1 \le A_{i,j} \le 3\)）。
接下来有 3 行，第 \(i\) 行包含 3 个数字 \(B_{i,1}\)、\(B_{i,2}\)、\(B_{i,3}\)，其中 \(B_{i,j}\) 表示 Alice 在上一局选择 \(i\) 且 Bob 选择 \(j\) 时，Bob 在本局的选择（\(1 \le B_{i,j} \le 3\)）。

output.ai: 输出两个数字。第一个数字应等于 Alice 获得的分数，第二个数字应等于 Bob 在进行 \(k\) 局游戏后的分数。

note.ai: 第二个样例中的游戏过程如下：
第四局和第七局由 Bob 获胜，第一局为和棋，其余各局由 Alice 获胜。
